CLOSE GATE CAUGHT A file_impact GAP, correctly, and this one is mine. The close refused because commit 2e7b10ad32 changes src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli_cli_ops.py, which the recorded file_impact did not declare.

That is accurate. When I filed this ticket I recorded file_impact as the test file alone, because I expected a pure test addition. The implementation then had to mark the ONE legitimate second composition - the Cloud adapter's defensive fit in add_comment - with a reasoned '# comment-fit-ok:' marker, which is a source edit. The guard has no way to sanction that site without touching it, so the declared scope was wrong from the start rather than having drifted.

file_impact now declares both paths. This is the THIRD instance of the same pattern in this run: 1cf6 (Scope named gc_trigger.py, file_impact omitted it), 7931 (Scope named bridge.py after review remediation, file_impact was never updated to match), and now a73e (file_impact recorded before implementation revealed a second required path). Scope and file_impact are maintained separately and nothing reconciles them until the close gate does - which is late, but it does catch it every time.
